# Data card: dataset_v2

**SIMULATED DATA - generated by a simplified mean-value engine model, not measured on any engine.** Nothing here has been validated against a real engine. Results obtained on these data rest on the simulator.

## Purpose

Training and honest testing of an uncertainty-aware virtual sensor for the exhaust gas temperature before the turbine of a large two-stroke marine-style engine, with a diesel-like fuel (n-dodecane surrogate) and methanol. The data also serve to test how the sensor behaves in regimes it did not see (high load, methanol at low load, cold ambient), with injected sensor faults, and when asked to abstain (30-40 % load, below the study range). The study range is 40-100 % load.

## Contents

Sampling 1 Hz, episodes of 1800 s. For every split two tables: `signals_<split>.parquet` (what a model may see) and `truth_<split>.parquet` (hidden plant states and noise-free values; for evaluation and gate checks only, never as a model input).

Model-visible columns: `fuel_code, n_rpm, m_fuel, p_scav, t_scav, n_tc, t_amb, p_amb`; target `t_exh_meas` (the measured, noisy, lagged exhaust sensor value). Units: speed rpm, fuel flow kg/s, pressures bar, temperatures K, turbocharger speed rpm. `fuel_code` 0 = diesel-like, 1 = methanol. Missing values (NaN) occur only at injected sensor dropouts: turbocharger-speed dropouts in every split, exhaust-temperature dropouts only in the fault split (the target is never missing in the other splits). `episodes.parquet` lists per-episode sensor biases, drift rates, fault type and a content digest; `events.parquet` lists dropouts and injected faults.

## How the data were generated

A quasi-steady plant solution (energy balance, speed-density air flow, turbine and compressor power balance, air cooler) is solved every second for a smooth load profile, followed by first-order lags for the slow signals, then a sensor model (lag, bias, drift, noise, quantisation, dropouts). Hidden fouling states of the turbocharger and the air cooler vary per episode. Every episode has its own seeded random generator, so any episode can be rebuilt from the configuration and its seed alone. Base seed 20261017.

Registry: 90 parameters: 15 sourced, 1 derived, 10 calibrated, 64 assumed. **All sensor noise levels, lag constants, health distributions and profile settings are assumed**, with a written rationale in `docs/PARAMETERS.md`. Methanol shares the diesel efficiency curve in the main data (assumption).

## Splits

| split | episodes | rows | fuel mix | load band | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| train | 220 | 396000 | diesel_like 60%, methanol 40% | diesel_like 0.40-0.90, methanol 0.55-0.90 | Fit models |
| validation | 150 | 270000 | diesel_like 60%, methanol 40% | diesel_like 0.40-0.90, methanol 0.55-0.90 | Choose features and tune models (never the test sets) |
| calibration | 150 | 270000 | diesel_like 60%, methanol 40% | diesel_like 0.40-0.90, methanol 0.55-0.90 | Conformal calibration and abstention thresholds |
| test_in_distribution | 100 | 180000 | diesel_like 60%, methanol 40% | diesel_like 0.40-0.90, methanol 0.55-0.90 | Calibration check under no shift (used once) |
| test_regime_high_load | 60 | 108000 | diesel_like 60%, methanol 40% | diesel_like 0.90-1.00, methanol 0.90-1.00 | Held-out regime, top load band above 90 percent (used once) |
| test_regime_methanol_low_load | 24 | 43200 | methanol 100% | methanol 0.40-0.55 | Held-out regime, methanol at 40 to 55 percent load (used once) |
| test_regime_cold_ambient | 24 | 43200 | diesel_like 60%, methanol 40% | diesel_like 0.40-0.90, methanol 0.55-0.90 | Held-out regime, cold ambient air (used once) |
| test_sensor_fault | 100 | 180000 | diesel_like 60%, methanol 40% | diesel_like 0.40-0.90, methanol 0.55-0.90 | Injected bias, drift and dropout on the exhaust temperature sensor (used once) |
| stress_low_load | 150 | 270000 | diesel_like 60%, methanol 40% | diesel_like 0.30-0.40, methanol 0.30-0.40 | Abstention stress test at 30 to 40 percent load. No accuracy or coverage is reported here because the labels are unverified. |
| stress_methanol_efficiency_minus | 20 | 36000 | methanol 100% | methanol 0.55-0.90 | Methanol efficiency 3 percent lower in the plant only (pre-specified stress test) |
| stress_methanol_efficiency_plus | 20 | 36000 | methanol 100% | methanol 0.55-0.90 | Methanol efficiency 3 percent higher in the plant only (pre-specified stress test) |
| test_regime_high_fouling | 240 | 432000 | diesel_like 60%, methanol 40% | diesel_like 0.40-0.90, methanol 0.55-0.90 | Held-out regime, high fouling of one component (used once). Two cohorts, reported separately; the other component stays in the training range. |

Episodes are never shared between splits; each split has its own seed id. The regime splits are held out by construction: training load is at most 0.90, methanol training load at least 0.55, training ambient temperatures above those of the cold split. Calibration and validation data are separate from training data. Fouling is capped at 0.50 in every split except `test_regime_high_fouling`, whose two cohorts (`tc_high`, `cooler_high`, 120 episodes each) have one component at 0.55 or more while the other stays capped.

## Changes from dataset_v1

dataset_v1 (hash ce417d33...) is retired. v2 differs only in fouling: all other random draws (fuel, ambient, load profile, sensor noise, faults) are identical by construction, because the same two Beta draws per episode are rescaled instead of resampled. The change was decided after seeing M0's residuals against fouling on a validation sample, for design coverage of the main hidden state; no learned model had been evaluated and no test split had been used for any model result.

## Known limits

* Fouling effects are assumed, not sourced. `test_regime_high_fouling` tests extrapolation within the simulator's own fouling law, not behaviour of real engines. Training fouling is capped at 0.50 (start range 0 to 0.45), which compresses the v1 training distribution (mean starting fouling of the turbocharger falls from about 0.19 to about 0.10, of the air cooler from about 0.23 to about 0.13).
* The simulator is a simplified steady-state-plus-lag model with generic parameters. The stroke, the air delivery law, the load dependence of exhaust temperature and the sizes of fouling and ambient effects are assumptions or unverified (see `docs/MODEL_CHOICES.md`, open items).
* Exhaust temperature may exceed 800 K at heavy fouling; no source covers that region.
* Sensor noise and lag values are plausible guesses, not instrument data sheets.
* Cold ambient is expected to be a weak shift: in earlier checks the nominal model absorbed ambient changes through the measured scavenge pressure and temperature. It is kept as a negative control.
* 30-40 % load data (`stress_low_load`) are used only for the abstention stress test; no accuracy or coverage is reported there.
* Methanol efficiency stress splits (-3 % / +3 %) test sensitivity to the shared-curve assumption; they come from the plant only.
* Wording rule: results "rest on the simulator", never "on verified physics".
